brief: The naming answers lawns, plots, water, paving, trees and living things, and returns '' for every wall — so at night, when the most legible things on screen are lit windows, the sill has nothing to say about any of them. Make a window under the pointer name itself and its cause: hit-test `WINDOWS[]` (and the row-64 live panes) in screen space the way `treeAt`/`livingAt` do, then read `windowLit`/`windowHours`/`HOMES` for the line — 'a lamp lit at 19.40, somebody came home', 'burning late', 'an early riser', 'dark: nobody home tonight', 'dark: gone to bed'. A front door gets its own line ('a front door; the lamp over it is lit'). Day-time the same window says 'a window' and nothing more.
successLooksLike: `probes/naming.mjs` gains a §8: at a midnight instant, hovering a pane that `windowLit` says is lit returns a line containing the cause; a dark pane returns the dark line; noon returns 'a window'. Nothing named today loses its name (the tree/living/paving cases in §1–§7 still pass).
avoid: Do not add a hint or an OFFERS entry — this rides the existing naming, which already has its invitation. Painter's order matters: a person standing in front of a window wins the hit. Read the register; never re-derive lit-ness in the sill.
